findings.text: The task log is missing the measurements the brief asks for. `pool-reclaim/task.jsonl` (in both the main tree and the worktree) has only the assign, skill and commit lines: no `pool-status.mjs` output (ask 1), no live reclaim result with the count of ready slots (ask 3), no `needs_restart` line and no landing line (ask 4). Run `node Servex/pool-status.mjs` and the live reclaim, and log both results before landing.

`reclaim()` never calls the new `verdict()` (Servex/Pool.js:240-275). Freeing still goes through `give_back()` → `landed()` → `on_base()`, so the FREE/KEPT that `pool-status.mjs` prints is a second copy of reclaim's rules. The two can drift: `verdict` does not model the 30-minute salvage path or a failed fast-forward. It would be simpler to have reclaim branch on `verdict()`, or have status call a dry-run of reclaim.

`give_back` runs `git branch -f landed/${id}-<date>` (Pool.js:~205). A second landing of the same slot on the same day moves that branch and drops the first one's reference. The content is already on the base, so nothing is lost in practice. Adding a time or a short sha to the name would keep both.

The brief said "the branch stays until the owner prunes". `worktree-down.mjs:84,128` still runs `branch -D` on `worktree/<slot>`, and the work survives under `landed/…` instead. That meets the intent, but the branch has a different name, which `doc/pool.md` does say.

The stale explicit-hold rule in `held()` (Pool.js:~286) goes beyond the brief. It is sensible and tested (the qf-8/fixer-1 case), but it is a second behaviour change in the same commit. The todo.md line does mention it.

Checked: `node Servex/Pool.test.mjs` passes in the worktree (three slots: two freed, one kept with its branch named, plus `landed/qf-2-*` reachable), and `node --check Servex/pool-status.mjs` is OK. The worktree has unrelated `files.jsonl` churn outside the fence. Make sure none of it is committed.

The real blockers were NOT 'holds work': an explicit hold() by a fixer gone since 10-14, and a dormant mastermind holding two slots.

MEASUREMENT after (same script, new rules): qf-8 FREE: stopped, clean, nothing ahead of the base (stale hold: holder gone 3 days) | qf-4 KEPT dormant | qf-7 KEPT dormant. 3 slots: 0 ready, 1 would be freed, 2 kept. qf-4's one commit is Servex-appended log lines (jsonl); it will read as on-base once its holder is not dormant.

Live reclaim NOT run: the live pool file belongs to the running Servex (in-memory slots, old Pool.js), a second writer would race it and kill qf-8's real server. Decision: prove with Pool.test.mjs (scratch repo: clean-stopped + landed-by-diff freed, unmerged kept with branch named, stale hold lets go) and the live dry-run above; after the restart the next sweep frees qf-8 so 1 slot goes ready (prepare() makes the fresh one). Alternative was a private Servex: heavy and its pool prefix differs.

findings.text: `node Servex/Pool.test.mjs` passes in the worktree (C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/pool-reclaim at 84edbb9a9). It covers all three slots the brief asked for (clean-stopped and merged-by-diff are freed, unmerged is kept with its branch named) plus the stale hold. `node --check Servex/pool-status.mjs` is ok.

The ask to "run reclaim on the live pool" was not met literally. The task log explains exactly why: the running Servex owns the pool file. The dry run with pool-status shows qf-8 would go FREE, and qf-4 and qf-7 stay KEPT because their holder is dormant. So 0 slots are ready until the restart, and 1 after. That meets the brief's "or say exactly why not" clause.

Servex/Pool.js:575: `landed()` now falls back to `on_base()`, which also changes `give_back()` for live callers (`return_worktree`). That is intended and it is conservative: a file that changed again on the base afterwards keeps the slot. Pool.js:604 `lines_on_base` compares a trimmed added line against base lines that are not trimmed. That is harmless, but only one of the two `has()` checks is needed.

Servex/Pool.js:620: `verdict()` copies the rules in `reclaim()` and does not call them, so pool-status could drift from what the sweep actually does. A simpler option is for `reclaim()` to branch on `verdict()` itself. The author weighed this and left it, and the test guards against drift.

Servex/Pool.js:287: the stale-`held_by` rule (a hold is released 12 h after its holder stopped or went) was not in the brief. The measurement shows it is the real fix for qf-8, though. It fails safe: a timestamp that does not parse gives NaN, so the slot stays held.

Servex/Pool.js:206: the work survives on `landed/<slot>-<date>-<sha>` instead of the slot's own branch, because worktree-down deletes that branch. This honours the brief's rule that nothing is discarded. pool.md documents it, and the brief's other wording ("the branch stays") is only met in spirit.
